newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 3.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 3.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Monday morning:

** Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda on Sunday told multinational corporations at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, to avoid using their strength to destroy or to "gobble up" the smaller companies. Instead, they should play a positive role by providing access to technology and capital, the Business Standard reports.
The paper quoted Gowda as saying developed countries
should desist from shutting out their markets through tariff and non-tariff barriers without adequate justification.

** The Confederation of Indian Industry-commissioned Omkar Gowswami draft report on corporate governance has recommended allowing takeover to be freely financed with market funds, the Economic Times reports.
The paper says the report recommended that financial

institutions withdraw from boards of companies where they have little or not debt exposure and where their shareholding is five percent or less, as well as permitting buy-back of shares and the issue of non-voting stock.

** India's year-on-year inflation rate measured by the wholesale price index fell to 7.48 percent in the week ending January 18 from 7.64 percent in the previous week, the Industry Ministry said on Sunday.
** The Indian rupee opened at 35.88/90 against the dollar on Monday, little changed from Friday's closing quote of 35.89/90, dealers said.
They said the rupee could breach 35.90-level if the
increased dollar demand seen last week continued.
** Soured expectations will drive Indian stocks down this week but brokers and analysts expect fresh demand to emerge at lower levels.
The benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange's .BSESN top-30
index fell 127.58 points, or 3.63 percent, to 3,382.47 on Friday -- losing 53.15 points or 1.55 percent in the week -- after the government dashed hopes of promised incentives.
